newsitem.title: UK: Hungary Cen bank sees higher GDP, lower inflation.
newsitem.headline: Hungary Cen bank sees higher GDP, lower inflation.

text.p: Hungary's gross domestic product is set to grow by three percent in 1997 compared with a flat 1996, Hungarian central bank president Gyorgy Suranyi told Reuters on Tuesday.
Suranyi added that inflation would fall from 20 percent at the end of this year, to 17 percent by the end of 1997.

He forecast Hungary's current account deficit would have shrunk to $1.5 billion to $1.6 billion by the end of 1996. "As a result of a reduction in Hungary's twin deficits we are able to consider reducing the 1.2 percent per month rate at which the forint is devalued," Suranyi said. "We will look at this after the first quarter of 1997."
